body.text: Mahāsāṃghikānāṃ prātimokṣasūtram
body.translated_text: The <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (code of individual liberation) of the <s>Mahāsāṃghikas</s>

body.text: namo vai bhagavate vītarāgāya //
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), who is free from passion.

children.translated_text: [Verse 1] By the <s>Buddha</s>, praised by kings of men and lords of gods, of vast renown among those who illuminate the three worlds,
the compassionate protector who walks among the people — by that wise one was the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of individual liberation) taught.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_2. taṃ prātimokṣaṃ bhavaduḥkhamokṣaṃ śruttvānudhīrāḥ sugatasya bhāṣitāṃ /
children.translated_text: [Verse 2] Having heard that <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, which is liberation from the suffering of existence, the wise ones, following the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One),
by restraining and guarding the six sense faculties, make an end of birth and death.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_3. cirasya labdhvā ratanāni trīṇi buddho yodaṃ māyikāñca śuddhāṃ /
children.translated_text: [Verse 3] Having long ago obtained the three jewels — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the pure <s>Saṃgha</s> —
having abandoned the fault of immorality, be of purified conduct and remain heedful!

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_4. śīlena yukto śramaṇo tireti śīlena yukto brāhmaṇo tireti /
children.translated_text: [Verse 4] The <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant) endowed with <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) crosses over; the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with <s>śīla</s> crosses over;

children.text: śīlena yukto naradevapūjyo śīlena yuktasya hi prātimokṣaṃ //
children.translated_text: one endowed with <s>śīla</s> is worshipped by gods and men; for the one endowed with <s>śīla</s>, there is the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_5. aneka buddhānumataṃ viśuddhaṃ śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhā dharaṇīvasāntaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Verse 5] The <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) approved by numerous <s>Buddhas</s>, pure, the foundation, firm as the earth,
that I shall recite in the midst of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, for the benefit of the world together with its gods.

body.text: upodghātaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Upodghāta</s> (Preface)

children.translated_text: [Verse 1] What use is life for those whose hearts
are covered by the nets of unwholesome roots, as the sky is covered by towering clouds?
But life is truly lived by those whose nets of unwholesome roots
swiftly dissolve, like darkness destroyed by the sun.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_2. kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te sāvadyaśīlacaritrāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse 2] What use is <s>Poṣadha</s> (observance day) for those whose conduct and morality are blameworthy,
who, trapped in the cage of old age and death, are devoured by the snares of <s>Māra</s> (the evil one)?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te anavadyaśīlacāritrāḥ /
children.translated_text: But <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those whose conduct and morality are blameless,
who are steadfast destroyers of old age and death, like the courageous ones who crush the army of <s>Māra</s>.
[Verse 3] What use is <s>Poṣadha</s> for the shameless, whose observances and morality are broken,
who delight in wrong livelihood, who speak as though they were immortal?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ larjjinām bhinnavṛttaśīlānāṃ /
children.translated_text: But <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for the conscientious, whose observances and morality are unbroken,
who delight in right livelihood, whose morality is pure in its underlying disposition.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_4. kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te duḥśī layāya karmmāntāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse 4] What use is <s>Poṣadha</s> for those of broken morality, whose actions lead to ruin,
who are cast out from the <s>Śāstṛ</s>'s (Teacher's) teaching like a corpse thrown out from the ocean?

children.text: kāryañca poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te tedhātuke atra prajñiptāḥ /
children.translated_text: But <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those who are established in the three realms of existence,
who are pure of hand like the open sky, whose minds are liberated.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_5. kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ ṣaḍindriyaṃ ye hi arakṣitaṃ nityaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Verse 5] What use is <s>Poṣadha</s> for those who never guard the six sense faculties,
who have fallen into the domain of <s>Māra</s>, who abandon the proper range of conduct?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ ṣaḍindriyaṃ ye hi surakṣitaṃ nityaṃ /
children.translated_text: But <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those who always well guard the six sense faculties,
who are liberated through the <s>Śāstṛ</s>'s (Teacher's) word, who delight in the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror).

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_6. kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ mātmaśīle hi ye svayaṃ vadanti /
children.translated_text: [Verse 6] What use is <s>Poṣadha</s> for those who themselves declare regarding their own morality,
yet are of broken morality — they and their fellow <s>brahmacārins</s> (spiritual companions), as well as their teacher and gods and men?

children.text: kāryañca poṣadhena teṣāṃ śīle hi nāsti gārhyaṃ /
children.translated_text: But <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those in whose morality there is nothing blameworthy,
who are beyond reproach everywhere among the wise in the world together with its gods.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_7. kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ virāgitaṃ śāstu śāsanaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Verse 7] What use is <s>Poṣadha</s> for those who are dispassionate toward the <s>Śāstṛ</s>'s (Teacher's) teaching,

children.text: ye hi āsevitā ca ye hi vipattīyo pañca cāpattīḥ //
children.translated_text: who have committed the five offenses and cultivated the transgressions?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ yuktānāṃ śāsane daśabalasya /
children.translated_text: But <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those who are devoted to the teaching of the <s>Daśabala</s> (One of Ten Powers),

children.text: saṃbuddhasya sarvvadarśinyo maitrīpadā ye hi paricīrṇṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: of the <s>Sambuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One), the all-seeing one, who have practiced the path of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_8. yeṣāṃ ca vasati hṛdaye śāstā dharmmo gaṇottamo /
children.translated_text: [Verse 8] Those in whose hearts dwell the <s>Śāstṛ</s> (Teacher), the <s>Dharma</s>, and the supreme <s>Gaṇa</s> (Community),

children.text: śikṣā uddeśo samvāso saṃtoṣo śāstuno vacanam //
children.translated_text: the training, the recitation, the communal life, contentment, and the word of the <s>Śāstṛ</s> —

children.text: teṣām poṣadho adya parityaktāni ye hi etāni /
children.translated_text: for them is this <s>Poṣadha</s> today. Those who have abandoned these things,
who serve the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of the Dharma) — for them there is the unconditioned knowledge.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_9. śuddhasya vai sadā hastaḥ sadā śuddhasya poṣadho /
children.translated_text: [Verse 9] For the pure one, the hand is always clean; for the pure one, the <s>Poṣadha</s> is always pure;
for the pure one, whose actions are clean — this always belongs to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_10. yāvatsūtraprātimokṣe so gaṇamadhya na bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: [Verse 10] As long as in the <s>Sūtra-Prātimokṣa</s> there shall be no discord in the midst of the community,
so long shall the true <s>Dharma</s> endure, and harmony in the supreme community.
[Verse 11] As long as there are those who recite and those who practice the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>,
so long shall the true <s>Dharma</s> endure, for the benefit of the entire world.
[Verse 12] Therefore, being assembled, united, and respectful,
attend to one another; realize the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of the Dharma).

body.text: nirvvāṇatā acyutasya damaśokamiti //
body.translated_text: That is <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — the imperishable, the taming, and the end of sorrow.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Einl. vastu-atikrāntāḥ suvihitāḥ śuddhanipuṇā antasamāpanno upaniṣaṇṇāḥ cāritrāḥ śalākāgaṇitā bhikṣuṇīmāprāptā ettarkajanāḥ / anāgatānāmāyuṣmanto bhikṣuṇācchanda pāriśuddhimārocethe / ārocitañca prativedetha-ko bhikṣu bhikṣuṇīnāṃ chandahārako nāsti cātra kaścidanupasaṃpannā nāsti uṣṇiyukto nāsti mātṛghātī nāsti pitṛghātī nāsti arhantaghātako / nāsti saṃghabhedako / nāsti tathāgatasya duṣtacittarudhiro khādake / nāsti bhikṣuṇī dūṣako / nāsti stainyasamvāsiko / nāsti nānāsamvāsiko nāsti asamvāsiko / nāsti kāyakrāntako (?) nāsti svayaṃ samuddiko / tadevaṃ samanvāharanta bhagavato śrāvakāṇāṃ nityaviśuddhānāṃ pariśuddhaśilānāṃ / śṛṇotu me bhante saṃgho adya saṃghasya cāturddaśiko vā sandhipoṣadho vā viśuddhinakṣatraṃ / ettakaṃ rāttasya niggataṃ / ettamavaśiṣṭaṃ / kiṃ saṃghasya pūrvvakṛtyaṃ / alpakṛtyo bhagavataḥ śrāvako saṃgho so bhavati / śṛṇotu me bhante saṃgho adya saṃghasya pāñcadaśiko poṣadho viśuddhinakṣatraṃ yadi saṃghasya prāptākālaṃ saṃgho imasmin pṛthivīpradeśe yavatakaṃ bhikṣusaṃghenābhigṛhītaṃ samantanavyāmamātraṃ atrāntare pāñcadaśikaṃ poṣadhaṃ kuryātprātimokṣaṃ ca sūtramuddiśeyyā, ovadikātrayājñapteḥ //
body.translated_text: [Procedure] The matter has been concluded. Those properly ordained, of pure and refined conduct, who have reached the final attainment, who are seated, whose conduct is established, who have been counted by voting sticks, from whom the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) have received permission, and from whom outsiders have departed — Venerable ones, announce the consent and declaration of purity of the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) who have not come. And make known what has been announced. Is there any <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who bears the consent of the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>? There is no one here who is unordained; there is no one with a head-covering; there is no matricide; there is no patricide; there is no killer of an <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one); there is no one who has caused a schism in the <s>Saṃgha</s>; there is no one who, with malicious intent, has shed the blood of a <s>Tathāgata</s>; there is no one who has defiled a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>; there is no one living in concealed ordination; there is no one of a different communion; there is no one excluded from communion; there is no one who has transgressed bodily; there is no one self-ordained. Thus bearing in mind the disciples of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), who are eternally pure, of purified morality — May the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> hear me: today is the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s fourteenth-day or conjunction <s>Poṣadha</s> (observance day), under an auspicious constellation. So much of the night has passed; so much remains. What is the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s preliminary business? The <s>Saṃgha</s> of the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s disciples has little business to attend to. May the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> hear me: today is the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s fifteenth-day <s>Poṣadha</s>, under an auspicious constellation. If the time has come for the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s> should perform the fifteenth-day <s>Poṣadha</s> in this area of ground encompassed by the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> within a boundary of the extent of an arm-span all around, and should recite the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> — by the authority of the triple announcement of the instructor.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Einl. kariṣyate bhante saṃgho imasmin pṛthivīpradeśe yāvatakaṃ bhikṣusaṃghenābhigṛhītaṃ samantana vyāmamātramatrāntare pāñcadaśikaṃ poṣadhaṃ prātimokṣaṃ ca sūtramuddiśiṣyati / kṣamate taṃ saṃghasya yasmāttūṣṇīmevametandhārayāmi / abhimukhaṃ kṣāmati jarāmaraṇaṃ kṣīyati jīvate priyaṃ hāyati saddharmmā astameti / dharmolko nirvvāpanti deśayitāraḥ / parīttā bhavanti pratipattāraḥ / gacchanti kṣaṇalavamuhurttarātrindivasamāsārddhamāsaṛtusamvatsarāḥ / girinadījalacapalacañcalopamā āyuḥ / saṃskārāmuddharttamapi nāvatiṣṭhante / apramādenāyuṣmante hi sampādayitavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / apramādādhigatānāṃ hi tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksambuddhānāṃ vaidhiḥ / apramādādhigato cānuttaro upadhi saṃkṣapīti vadāma / tenāpramādenāyuṣmante hi saṃpādayitavyaṃ / daśānvasan sampaśyamānāstathāgatā'rhantaḥ samyak saṃbuddhāḥ // śrāvakāṇāmadhiśīlaṃ śikṣaṃ padaṃ prajñāpayanti / pratimokṣa ca sūtramuddiśanti / katamāndaśa / saṃyyathīdaṃ / saṃghasaṃgrahāya saṃghasuṣṭhutāya / durmatkuṇnāṃ pudgalānānnigrahāya peśalānāñca bhikṣuṇā phāsu vihārāya / aprasannānāṃ pramādāya / prasannānāñca trayobhāvāya dṛṣṭadhārmikāṇāmāśravāṇāṃ nirghātāya samparāyikāṇāmāśravāṇāmāpatyāmananuśravaṇatāya / yathemaṃ syātpra vacanaṃ virakṣitikaṃ vā bhujanyaṃvivṛtaṃ suprakāśitaṃ yāvandevamanuṣyeṣviti / imāndaśāncavasānsaṃpaśyamānāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyak sambuddhāḥ / śrāvakāṇāmadhiśīlaṃ śikṣapadaṃ prajñāpayanti / pratimokṣañca sutramuddiśanti /
body.translated_text: [Procedure continued] The venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> will perform the fifteenth-day <s>Poṣadha</s> in this area of ground encompassed by the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> within a boundary of the extent of an arm-span all around, and will recite the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s>. The <s>Saṃgha</s> accepts this; therefore I hold it thus in silence. It should be accepted face to face: old age and death waste away; life and what is dear diminish; the true <s>Dharma</s> sets like the sun; the torch of the <s>Dharma</s> is extinguished; the teachers become few; those who practice become scarce. Moments, instants, hours, nights, days, fortnights, half-months, seasons, and years pass away. Life is like the swift, flickering current of a mountain river. <s>Saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations), even when sustained, do not endure. Therefore, venerable ones, you must strive with diligence! For what reason? Because diligence is the means by which <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> (Perfectly Awakened Ones) have attained realization. And we declare that the unsurpassed state, the cessation of the substrata of existence, is attained through diligence. Therefore, venerable ones, you must strive with diligence. Seeing these ten reasons, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> establish for their disciples the training rules pertaining to higher morality, and recite the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s>. What are the ten? They are as follows: for the restraint of the <s>Saṃgha</s>; for the well-being of the <s>Saṃgha</s>; for the suppression of ill-behaved persons; for the comfortable dwelling of well-behaved <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks); for inspiring faith in those without faith; for the increase of faith in those who have faith; for the destruction of <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) pertaining to this present life; for preventing the arising of <s>āśravas</s> pertaining to future lives; so that this teaching may be long-lasting, well-guarded, widely enjoyed, well-disclosed, and well-illuminated among gods and men. Seeing these ten reasons, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> establish for their disciples the training rules pertaining to higher morality, and recite the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Einl. prātimokṣamāyuṣmānto sūtramuddiśiṣyāmi / tāṃ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣyāmi / paśya vo siyāpattiḥ so'viṣkarottu / asantīye āpattīye tūṣṇī bhavitavyaṃ / tūṣṇīmbhāvena / kho punarāyuṣmanto pariśuddha iti vedayiṣyāmi yathā kho punarāyuṣmanto pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ pṛcchitasya bhikṣusya vyākaraṇaṃ bhavati / evameva mevaṃ rūpāye bhikṣuparyāye yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanuśrāvayiṣyati / yo punabhikṣu evaṃ rūpāye bhikṣuparyāye yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanuśrāviyamāṇo smaramāṇo santī māpattīnnāviṣkaroti / saṃprajñānaṃ mṛṣāvādo me bhavati / saṃprajānamṛṣāvādo kho punarāyuṣmanto antarāyiko dhammo ukto bhagavatā / tasmātsmaramāṇena bhikṣuṇa āpanne viśuddhi prekṣeṇa santī āpattī āviṣkarttavyā / āviṣkṛtvā ca me phāsu bhavati no anāviṣkṛtvā / nidānaṃ //
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, I shall recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of discipline) sūtra. Listen to it well and carefully, and attend to it in your minds; I shall speak. Should you have any offense, let him disclose it. In the absence of an offense, one should remain silent. By the silence of the venerable ones, I shall know that they are pure. Just as when a <s>bhikṣu</s> is questioned individually, there is a declaration — in exactly the same way, in such an assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, I shall proclaim up to three times. If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, when this is being proclaimed up to three times in such an assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, remembering an existing offense, does not disclose it — there is a deliberate falsehood on his part. And deliberate falsehood, venerable ones, has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be an obstructive thing (<s>antarāyika dharma</s>). Therefore, a <s>bhikṣu</s> who remembers, who has committed an offense, who desires purification, should disclose an existing offense. For having disclosed it, there is ease for me; not having disclosed it, there is not. [This concludes] the introduction (<s>nidāna</s>).

body.text: I. THE FOUR PARAJIKA DHARMAS.
body.translated_text: I. The four <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) rules.

body.text: ime kho punarāyuṣmanto catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmā anvarddhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśamāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these four <s>pārājika</s> rules come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> sūtra every half-month.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Pār.1. yo punabhikṣu bhikṣuṇā śikṣā sāmīcīsamāpanno śikṣāmāpratyākhyāya daurvvalyamanāviṣkṛtvā maithunaṃ grāmyadharmmaṃ pratiṣeveya antamaśato tiryagyonigatāyamapi sārddhamayaṃ bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavatyasaṃvāsyo na labhate bhikṣu hi sārddha saṃvāsaṃ /
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, having entered upon the training and the proper conduct along with <s>bhikṣus</s>, without having renounced the training and without having disclosed his weakness, should engage in sexual intercourse — the vulgar practice — even with a female animal, this <s>bhikṣu</s> is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion (<s>asaṃvāsya</s>). He does not obtain the right to live together with <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_idaṃ bhagavatā veśālīyaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ pañcavarṣābhisaṃbuddhena hemante pakṣe pañcame divase dvādaśame pūre bhuktamuttarāmukhaniṣaṇṇena dvyarddhapauruṣāyāṃcchāyāyāṃ āyuṣmantaṃ yaśikakalandakaputramārabhya imasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptirdharmo yathā praṇihitasya ca yā anuvartanatā ayamucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule (<s>śikṣāpada</s>) was established by the <s>Bhagavān</s> at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, five years after His enlightenment, in the winter, in the fifth fortnight, on the twelfth day, after the meal, seated facing north, when the shadow was two-and-a-half person-lengths, with reference to the venerable <s>Yaśika Kalandakaputra</s>. The establishment of this training rule is the <s>dharma</s>; and conformity to what has been laid down is called the subsidiary rule (<s>anudharma</s>).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Pār.2. yo punabhikṣū grāmādvā araṇyādvā adinnamanyātakaṃ stainyasaṃskāramādiyeya yathārūpeṇādinnādānena jāno gṛhītvā hanyemvā vadhemvā pravrājemvā hambho puruṣa corosi bālosi mūḍhosi stainyosīti vā vadem tathārūpaṃ bhikṣūradinnamādeyamāno ayame bhikṣūḥ pārājiko bhavatyasamvāsyo na labhate bhikṣū hi sārddhasaṃvāsaṃ /
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, from a village or from a forest, should take what is not given — belonging to another — with the intention of stealing, in such a manner of taking what is not given that a king, having seized the thief, would execute him, imprison him, or banish him, saying: 'Hey, fellow! You are a thief, you are a fool, you are confused, you are a robber!' — a <s>bhikṣu</s> taking what is not given in such a manner is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain the right to live together with <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_idaṃ bhagavatā rājagṛhe śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ ṣaḍvarṣābhisambuddhena hemante pakṣe dvitīvase navame paścādbhuktaṃ purastānmukhaniṣaṇṇena / arddhatīyapauruṣāyāṃ cchāyāyāmāyuṣmantaṃ dhanikaṃ kuṃbhakārajātiyamārabhya rājānañca śreṇīyaṃ bimbasāraṃ pāṃsukulikaṃ ca bhikṣu / imasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptirdharmo yathā praṇihitasya ca yā anuvarttanatā ayamucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule was established by the <s>Bhagavān</s> at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, six years after His enlightenment, in the winter, in the second fortnight, on the ninth day, after the meal, seated facing east, when the shadow was two-and-a-half person-lengths, with reference to the venerable <s>Dhanika</s> of the potter caste and King <s>Śreṇiya Bimbisāra</s> and a <s>bhikṣu</s> who wore robes from dust-heaps (<s>pāṃsukūlika</s>). The establishment of this training rule is the <s>dharma</s>; and conformity to what has been laid down is called the subsidiary rule.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Pār.3. yo punabhikṣuḥ svahastaṃ manuṣyavigrahaṃ jīvitād vyāparopeya śastrahārakaṃ vāsya paryeyeya maraṇāya cainaṃ samādāpeya maraṇāvaṇṇaṃ vāsya saṃvaṇṇeya hambho puruṣa kinte iminā pāpakena durjjīvitena viśjīvitena mṛtante jīvitācchreyo iti cittamalaṃ cittasaṃkalpamanekaparyāyeṇa maraṇāya cainaṃ samādāpeya maraṇavaṇṇavāsya saṃvaṇṇeya so ca puruṣo tenopakrameṇa kālaṃ kuryānnānyena ayaṃ pi bhikṣūḥ pārājiko bhavatyasaṃvāsyo na labhate bhikṣuhi sārdhasaṃvāsaṃ /
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s> should intentionally deprive a human being of life, or should seek a weapon-bearer for him, or should incite him to death, or should praise death to him [saying]: 'Hey, fellow! What use is this wretched, miserable life to you? Death is better for you than life!' — and with such mental intent and mental resolve, in various ways, should incite him to death or praise death to him, and that person should die by that means and not by another — this <s>bhikṣu</s> too is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain the right to live together with <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: idaṃ bhagavatā veśālīyaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ ṣaḍvarṣo'bhisaṃmbuddhena hemante pakṣe tṛtīye divase daśame paścād bhuktaṃ purastābhimukhāniṣaṇṇena arddhatṛtīyena pauruṣāyāṃcchāyāyāṃ sambahulāna gilānopasthāpakān bhikṣūnārabhya mṛgadaṇḍikaṃ ca parivrajakamimasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptirddharmo yathā praṇihitasya ca yā anuvarttanatā ayamucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule was established by the <s>Bhagavān</s> at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, six years after His enlightenment, in the winter, in the third fortnight, on the tenth day, after the meal, seated facing forward, when the shadow was two-and-a-half person-lengths, with reference to several <s>bhikṣus</s> who attended the sick and the wanderer (<s>parivrājaka</s>) <s>Mṛgadaṇḍika</s>. The establishment of this training rule is the <s>dharma</s>; and conformity to what has been laid down is called the subsidiary rule.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Pār.4. yo punabhikṣuranabhijānanuparijānannātmopanāyikamuttari manuṣya [dharmaṃ] it / ayaṃ pi bhikṣūḥ dharmmamalamāryajñānadaśanaṃ viśeṣādhiśeṣādhigama pratijāneya iti jānāmi iti paśyāmīti / so tadapareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇo, vā a[sa] manugrāhiyamāṇo vā āpanno viśuddhiprokṣo evamavaci / ajānannevāhamāyuṣmanto avaci jānāmi / ayaṃ pi paśyāmīti iti tucchaṃ mṛṣāvilāpamanyatrābhimānāt / ayaṃ pi bhikṣūḥ pārājiko bhavatyasaṃvāsyo na labhate bhikṣūhi sārddhaṃsaṃ [vāsaṃ] /
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, without knowing and without understanding, should claim for himself a superhuman attainment (<s>uttarimanuṣyadharma</s>) — a noble knowledge and vision — [saying] 'Thus I know, thus I see,' and he, at a later time, whether being examined or not being examined, having committed the offense and seeking purification, should say thus: 'Venerable ones, without knowing I said "I know," without seeing I said "I see" — [it was] empty, false prattle,' — unless it was through overestimation (<s>abhimāna</s>) — this <s>bhikṣu</s> too is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain the right to live together with <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: idaṃ bhagavatā śrāvastīyaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ ṣaḍvarṣābhisaṃbuddhena hemante pakṣe catuththe divase trayodaśame pūre bhuktaṃ uttarāmu khaniṣaṇṇena arddhantha pauruṣāyāṃcchāyāyāṃ sambahulān grāmavāsikā bhikṣunārabhya ābhimānikaṃ ca bhikṣu imasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptirddharmo yathāpraṇihitasya ca yā anuvarttanatā ayamucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule was established by the <s>Bhagavān</s> at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, six years after His enlightenment, in the winter, in the fourth fortnight, on the thirteenth day, before the meal, seated facing north, when the shadow was one-and-a-half person-lengths, with reference to several <s>bhikṣus</s> dwelling in a village and a <s>bhikṣu</s> who acted from overestimation. The establishment of this training rule is the <s>dharma</s>; and conformity to what has been laid down is called the subsidiary rule.

body.text: udyānaṃ // [1] maithunaṃ [2] adinnādānaṃ [3] vadho manuṣyavigrahaṃ [4] syātkṛtena cottarimanuṣyadharma pratijānatīti //
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>): [1] sexual intercourse, [2] taking what is not given, [3] killing a human being, [4] and falsely claiming superhuman attainment.

body.text: uddiṣtāḥ // kho punarāyuṣmano catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmāḥ / yeṣāṃ bhikṣuritonyatarāmāpattimāpadyetvā pārājiko bhavatyasamvāsyo na labhate hi bhikṣuhi sārddhasaṃvāsaṃ / yathāpūrvve tathā paścādyathāpaścāttathā pūrvve pārājiko bhavatyasamvāsyo na labhate bhikṣu hi [sārdhaṃ] saṃvāsaṃ / tatrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / dvitīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāstṛtīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ pariśuddhātrāyuṣmanto yasmāttūṣṇīmeva metaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the four <s>pārājika</s> rules have been recited. Any <s>bhikṣu</s> who commits any one of these offenses is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain the right to live together with <s>bhikṣus</s>. As before, so after; as after, so before — he is defeated, no longer in communion. He does not obtain the right to live together with <s>bhikṣus</s>. Therein I ask the venerable ones: 'Are you pure?' A second time I ask the venerable ones: 'Are you pure?' A third time I ask the venerable ones: 'Are you pure?' The venerable ones are pure herein, since they are silent. Thus I understand it.

body.text: II. THE THIRTEEN SAMGHATISESA DHARMAS.
body.translated_text: II. The thirteen <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (rules entailing formal meeting of the community) rules.

body.text: ime punarāyuṣmanto trayodaśa saṃghātiśeṣā dharmā anvaddharmāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddheśamāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these thirteen <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> rules come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> sūtra every half-month.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.1. saṃcetanikā ye śukrasya viśṛṣtīye anyatra svapnāntareṃ saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: Any intentional emission of semen, except during a dream, is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (offense requiring formal meeting of the community).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.2. yo punabhikṣu otīṇṇā vipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmeṇa sārddhaṃ kāyasaṃsaṃggaṃ samāpadyeya saṃyathīdaṃ hastagrahaṇaṃ vā veṇīgrahaṇamvā anyatarānyatarasya vā punaraṅgajātasya prāmodya śaparāsopiṇaṃ śādiyeya saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, overcome by desire, with a perverted mind, should engage in bodily contact with a woman — such as holding hands, holding her braid, or touching and caressing any part of her body — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.3. yo punabhikṣu otīṇṇā viparītena cittena mātṛgrāmaṃ dusthūlāya vācāya obhāṣeya pāpikāya maithunāya saṃvītāya saṃyathīdaṃ yuvāṃ yuvāṃ yuvatīti saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, overcome by desire, with a perverted mind, should address a woman with coarse words — wicked words pertaining to sexual intercourse — such as 'You are young, you are young, you are a young woman' — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.4. yo punabhikṣu otīṇṇo vipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmasya antike ātmikāye paricaryāye vaṇṇaṃ bhāṣeya etadagraṃ bhagini paricaryāṇāṃ yā mādṛśaṃ śramaṇaṃ śīlavantaṃ kalyāṇadharmaṃ brahmacāriṃ etena dharmeṇa upasthiheya paricareya yaduta maithunopasaṃhiteneti saṃghātiśeṣo //
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, overcome by desire, with a perverted mind, should speak in the presence of a woman praising the service of his own person [saying]: 'Sister, this is the highest of services — that one should attend to and serve a renunciant like me, who is virtuous and of good conduct, who lives the holy life, with this practice' — meaning one connected with sexual intercourse — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.5. yo punabhikṣuḥ saṃcaritraṃ samāpadyeya striyāye vā puruṣasyopasaṃhareya puruṣyasya vā sataṃ striyāye upasaṃhareya jāyattanena vā jārttanena vā antamasato bhikṣuṇi kāyāmapi saṃghātiśeṣo //
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣu</s> should act as a go-between — conveying a woman's [message] to a man or a man's [message] to a woman — whether for the purpose of marriage or of an illicit liaison, even if to a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.6. svayaṃ cāyikāya bhikṣuṇā kuṭī kārāpayamāṇena asvābhikātmoddeśikāṃ kuṭīkārāpayitavyā / tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ dīrdhaso dvādaśavitastīyo sugatavitastinā / tiryaka saptāntaraṃ bhikṣu cānonābhinetavyā vastudeśanāya te hi bhikṣu hi vastu deśayitavyaṃ / anārambhāṃ saparikramaṇaṃ sārambhe ce bhikṣu vastusminnaparikramaṇe svayaṃ yācikāya kuṭīṃ kārāpeyaṃ / asvābhikāmātmoddeśikaṃ bhikṣustānābhineya vastudesanāya / pramāṇaṃ vā atikrameya adeśite vastusminnaparikramaṇe saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 6. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a hut built by his own begging, he should have it built without a patron, not designated for himself. The measure for this is: twelve spans in length by the <s>Sugata</s>-span, seven [spans] in width. <s>Bhikṣus</s> should be brought [to the site] for the inspection of the site; those <s>bhikṣus</s> should inspect the site. [It should be] without obstruction, with a surrounding pathway. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> has a hut built by his own begging on a site with obstruction and without a surrounding pathway, without a patron, not designated for himself — if <s>bhikṣus</s> are not brought for the inspection of the site, or if the measure is exceeded, or on a site that has not been inspected, without a surrounding pathway — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (offense requiring formal meeting of the <s>Saṃgha</s>).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.7. mahālakaṃ bhikṣuṇā vihāraṃ [kārā] pathamāṇena sasvāmikakātmoddeśikaṃ bhikṣuvānenābhinetavyā vastudeśanāya te hi bhikṣū hi vastu deśayitavyaṃ / anārambhaḥ saparikramaṇaṃ sārambhe ce bhikṣūṃ vastusminnaparikramaṇaṃ mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārāpeya sasvāmikamātmoddeśikaṃ bhikṣunvā nābhineya vastudeśanā ya adeśite vastusminnaparikramaṇe saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 7. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a large <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) built — with a patron, designated for himself — <s>bhikṣus</s> should be brought [to the site] for the inspection of the site; those <s>bhikṣus</s> should inspect the site. [It should be] without obstruction, with a surrounding pathway. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> has a large <s>vihāra</s> built on a site with obstruction and without a surrounding pathway — with a patron, designated for himself — if <s>bhikṣus</s> are not brought for the inspection of the site, or on a site that has not been inspected, without a surrounding pathway — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.8. yo punabhikṣū bhikṣusya duṣto doṣātkupito anāttamano śuddhaṃ bhikṣūmanāpatikamamūlakena pārājikena dharmeṇa anudhvaṃseya appeva nāma imaṃ bhikṣūṃ brahmacaryāto cyāveyanti / so tadapareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā asamanugrāhiyamāṇo vā amūlakameva tamadhikaraṇaṃ bhavati / amūlakasya ca adhikaraṇasya ca adharmo upādinno bhavati / bhikṣu ca doṣe pratiṣṭhihati / doṣādavacāmīti saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 8. If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, being corrupt, angry from hostility, displeased, should charge a pure <s>bhikṣu</s> who is without offense with a baseless <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offense, [thinking]: 'Perhaps I may cause this <s>bhikṣu</s> to fall from the holy life' — and if at a later time, whether being examined or not being examined, that case is indeed baseless, and from the baseless case an unlawful [charge] has been taken up, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> stands in hostility [and says]: 'I speak from hostility' — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.9. yo punabhikṣū bhikṣusya duṣto doṣātkupito anāttamano anyabhāgīyasyādhikaraṇasya kiñcideva lesāmātrakaṃ dharmamupādāya aparājikaṃ bhikṣūṃ parājikeṇa dharmeṇa anudhvaṃseya appeva nāma imaṃ bhikṣuṃ brahmacaryāto cyāveyanti / so tadapareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā asamanugrāhiyamāṇo vā anyabhāgīyameva tamadhikaraṇaṃ bhavati / anyabhāgīyasya cādhikaraṇasya keci [deva] lesāmātrako dharmo upādinno bhavati / bhikṣu ca doṣe pratiṣṭhahati doṣādavacāmīti saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 9. If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, being corrupt, angry from hostility, displeased, should take up merely some slight aspect of a matter belonging to a different category and charge a non-<s>pārājika</s> <s>bhikṣu</s> with a <s>pārājika</s> offense, [thinking]: 'Perhaps I may cause this <s>bhikṣu</s> to fall from the holy life' — and if at a later time, whether being examined or not being examined, that case indeed belongs to a different category, and from the case belonging to a different category only some slight aspect of the matter has been taken up, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> stands in hostility [and says]: 'I speak from hostility' — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.10. yo punabhikṣuḥ samagrasya saṃghasya bhedāya parākrameya bhedanasamvarttanīyamvā'dhikaraṇaṃ / samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheya so bhikṣu bhikṣuhi evamasya vacanīyo mā āyuṣman samagrasya saṃghasya bhedāya parākramehi / bhedana samvarttanīyamvā adhikaraṇaṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭhāhi / sametta āyuṣmānsārddhaṃ saṃghena samagrohi saṃgho sahito sammodamāno avivadamāno ekuddeśo kṣīrodakī bhūto śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ dīpayamāno sukhaṃ ca phāsuñca viharati / evaṃ ca sa bhikṣū bhikṣū hi vucyamāno taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareya ityetaṃ kuśalaṃ / so ca pratinissareya so bhikṣū bhikṣū hi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyo samanubhāṣitavyo tasya vastusya pratinissaggāya yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇo vā / taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareya ityetaṃ kuśalaṃ no ca pratinissareya tameva vastusamādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheya saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 10. If any <s>bhikṣu</s> should exert himself for the splitting of a united <s>Saṃgha</s>, or should take up, grasp, and persist in a matter conducive to splitting — that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Venerable one, do not exert yourself for the splitting of a united <s>Saṃgha</s>! Do not take up, grasp, and persist in a matter conducive to splitting! Let the venerable one be united with the <s>Saṃgha</s>, for when the <s>Saṃgha</s> is united, harmonious, not quarreling, having one recitation, blended like milk and water, illuminating the Teacher's teaching, it dwells in happiness and comfort.' If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, being thus addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, should relinquish that matter — that is good. If he does not relinquish — that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be admonished and exhorted by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishing of that matter. If, being admonished and exhorted up to three times, he relinquishes that matter — that is good. If he does not relinquish, [but] takes up, grasps, and persists in that very matter — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.11. tasya kho punabhikṣusya bhikṣusahāyakā bhonti / eko vā dvau vā trayo vā sambahulā vā vagavādakā anuvattakāḥ samanuṣyāḥ saṃghabhedāya te bhikṣū tānbhikṣūnevaṃ vadeyya mā āyuṣmanto etaṃ bhikṣuṃ kiñcidvadatha / kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakamvā / dharmmavādī caiṣo bhikṣū vinayavādī caiṣo bhikṣū asmākaṃ caiṣo bhikṣūcchandañca rūciñca samādāya pragṛhya vyavaharati / ya caitasya bhikṣūsya kṣamate ca rocate ca asmākamapi taṃ kṣamate ca rocate ca jānan caiṣo bhikṣu bhāṣate no ajānan / te bhikṣū bhikṣū hi evamasya vacanīyā māyuṣmanto evaṃ vadatha na eṣo bhikṣū dharmavādī na eṣo bhikṣū vinayavādī adharmavādī caiṣo bhikṣū avinayavādī caiṣo bhikṣū ajānan caiṣo bhikṣū bhāṣate no jānan / mā āyuṣmanto saṃghabhedaṃ rocenta saṃghasāmagrīmevāyuṣmanto rocanta / samenta āyuṣmanto sārdhaṃ saṃghena samagro hi saṃgho sahito sammodamāno avivadamāno ekuddeśo kṣīrodakī bhūto śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ dīpayamāno sukhaṃ ca phāsuṃ ca viharati / evañca te bhikṣu bhikṣuhi vucyamānāstamvastuṃ pratinissarea ityetaṃ kuśalaṃ no ca pratinissarea te bhikṣū bhikṣū hi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyāḥ samanubhāṣitavyāḥ / tasya vastusya pratinissaggāya yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇā vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇā vā tamvastuṃ pratinissarea itaṃ kuśalaṃ no ca pratinissareṃsu tameva ca vastuṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheya saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 11. If that <s>bhikṣu</s> has <s>bhikṣu</s>-companions — one, two, three, or several — who are partisan speakers, followers, associates in the splitting of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, those <s>bhikṣus</s> should address those <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Venerable ones, do not say anything to this <s>bhikṣu</s>, whether good or bad! For this <s>bhikṣu</s> is one who speaks <s>Dharma</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> is one who speaks <s>Vinaya</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> takes up, grasps, and acts according to our wishes and preferences. What is acceptable and agreeable to this <s>bhikṣu</s> is also acceptable and agreeable to us. This <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks knowingly, not unknowingly.' Those <s>bhikṣus</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Venerable ones, do not speak thus! This <s>bhikṣu</s> does not speak <s>Dharma</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> does not speak <s>Vinaya</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks against <s>Dharma</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks against <s>Vinaya</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks unknowingly, not knowingly. Venerable ones, do not approve of the splitting of the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Let the venerable ones approve of the harmony of the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Let the venerable ones be united with the <s>Saṃgha</s>, for when the <s>Saṃgha</s> is united, harmonious, not quarreling, having one recitation, blended like milk and water, illuminating the Teacher's teaching, it dwells in happiness and comfort.' If those <s>bhikṣus</s>, being thus addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, relinquish that matter — that is good. If they do not relinquish — those <s>bhikṣus</s> should be admonished and exhorted by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishing of that matter. If, being admonished and exhorted up to three times, they relinquish that matter — that is good. If they do not relinquish, [but] take up, grasp, and persist in that very matter — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA.12. bhikṣuḥ kho punadūrvvacakajātīyo bhoti so uddeśaparyāpanne hi śikṣāpade hi bhikṣu hi śikṣāyāṃ sahadharmeṇa sahavinayena vucya māno ātmānamavacanīyaṃ karoti / so evamāha / mā māṃ āyuṣmanto kiñcidvadatha kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā / ahamapyāyuṣmantānāṃ na kiñcid pracchomi / kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā viramanvāyuṣmanto mama vacanāya / so bhikṣū bhikṣū hi evamasya vacanīyo mā āyuṣmannuddeśaparyāpanne hi śikṣāpade hi bhikṣū hi śikṣāyāṃ sahadharmeṇa saha vinayena vucyamāno ātmānamavacanīyaṃ karo hi vacanīyam vāyuṣmānātmānaṃ karottu bhikṣu pi āyuṣmantamvakṣanti śikṣāyāṃ sahadharmeṇa sahavina [yena] āyuṣmānapi bhikṣūnvadantu śikṣayā sahadharmeṇa sahavinayena / evaṃ samvaddhā kho punastasya bhagavato tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyak sambuddhasya yathā yadidamasya manyasya vacanīyā anyo nyāpatti vyutthāpanīyā / evaṃ ca so bhikṣū bhikṣū hi vucyamāno taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareya ityetaṃ kuśalaṃ no ca pratinissareya so bhikṣū bhikṣū hi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyo samanubhāṣitavyo tasya vastusya pratinissaggāya yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇo vābhivastuṃ pratinissareya ityetaṃ kuśalaṃ no ca pratinissareya tameva vastuṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheya saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 12. A <s>bhikṣu</s> may be of a difficult-to-admonish nature. When, regarding the training rules included in the recitation, <s>bhikṣus</s> admonish him in the training in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, he makes himself one who cannot be spoken to. He speaks thus: 'Venerable ones, do not say anything to me, whether good or bad! I too shall not ask the venerable ones anything, whether good or bad. Refrain, venerable ones, from [trying to] admonish me!' That <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Venerable one, when, regarding the training rules included in the recitation, <s>bhikṣus</s> admonish you in the training in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, do not make yourself one who cannot be spoken to! Let the venerable one make himself one who can be spoken to! The <s>bhikṣus</s> will also speak to the venerable one in the training, in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Let the venerable one also speak to the <s>bhikṣus</s> in the training, in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. For thus has the assembly of the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, grown — namely, by mutual admonition and mutual rehabilitation from offenses.' If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, being thus addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, relinquishes that matter — that is good. If he does not relinquish — that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be admonished and exhorted by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishing of that matter. If, being admonished and exhorted up to three times, he relinquishes that matter — that is good. If he does not relinquish, [but] takes up, grasps, and persists in that very matter — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA. bhikṣu kho punaranyataraṃ grāmamvā nagaramvā nigamamvā upaniśrāya viharanti / kuladūṣakāḥ pāpasamācārāsteṣānte pāpakāḥ samācārā dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca kulānyapi duṣtāni dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca kuladūṣakāśca punarbhavanti / pāpasamācārāḥ te bhikṣū bhikṣū hi evamasya va canīyāḥ / āyuṣmantānāṃ khalu pāpakāḥ samācārāḥ dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca kulānyapi duṣtāni dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca / kuladūṣakāśca punarāyuṣmantaḥ pāpasamācārāḥ prakramanvāyuṣmanto imasmādāvāsādalamvā iha vāseneti / evaṃ ca te bhikṣū bhikṣū hi vucyamānāste bhikṣū tānbhikṣune vadea cchandagāmī cāyuṣmānto saṃgho doṣagāmī cāyuṣmanto saṃgho mohagāmī cāyuṣmanto saṃgho bhayagāmī cāyuṣmanto saṃgho saṃgho ca tāhi tādṛśikāhi āpattīhi / ekatyān bhikṣūn pravrājeti ekatyānbhikṣunna pravrājeti te bhikṣū bhikṣū hi evaṃmasya vacanīyāḥ / mā āyuṣmanto evaṃ vada na ca bhikṣū na saṃgho cchandagāmī / na saṃgho doṣagāmī na saṃgho mohagāmī / na saṃgho bhayagāmī / na ca saṃgho tāhi tādṛśikāhi āpattīhi / ekatyānbhikṣūn pravrājeti ekatyānbhikṣūnna pravrājeti / āyuṣmantānāmeva khalamāpakaḥ samācārā dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca kulānyapi duṣtāni dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca kuladūṣakāśca punarāyuṣmantaḥ grāmasamācārāḥ prakramanvāyuṣmanto imasmādāvāsādalamvā iha vāseneti evaṃ ca bhikṣū bhikṣū hi vucyamānābhivastupratinissarea ityetaṃ kuśalaṃ no ca pratinissarea te bhikṣū bhikṣū hi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyā samanubhāṣitavyāstasya vastusya pratinissaggāya yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇā vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇā vā taṃ vastuṃ pratinissarea ityetaṃ kuśalaṃ no ca pratinissarea ime ca vastuṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭhea saṃghātiśeṣo //
body.translated_text: If monks dwell near a certain village, town, or market town, and they are corrupters of families (<s>kuladūṣaka</s>) and of evil conduct — their evil conduct is both seen and heard, and the families they have corrupted are both seen and heard — and they are furthermore corrupters of families and of evil conduct, those monks should be addressed by the monks thus: 'The venerable ones' evil conduct is both seen and heard, and the families corrupted are both seen and heard. The venerable ones are corrupters of families and of evil conduct. Let the venerable ones depart from this dwelling; enough of dwelling here.' When those monks are thus addressed (<s>vucyamānā</s>) by the monks, those monks say to those monks: 'The venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> acts out of desire, the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> acts out of hatred, the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> acts out of delusion, the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> acts out of fear. The <s>Saṃgha</s> banishes some monks for such offenses but does not banish others.' Those monks should be addressed by the monks thus: 'Let the venerable ones not speak thus. The monks are not biased, the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not act out of desire, the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not act out of hatred, the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not act out of delusion, the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not act out of fear. The <s>Saṃgha</s> does not banish some monks for such offenses while not banishing others. It is indeed the venerable ones' own evil conduct that is both seen and heard, and the families corrupted are both seen and heard. The venerable ones are corrupters of families and of evil conduct. Let the venerable ones depart from this dwelling; enough of dwelling here.' When those monks, being thus addressed (<s>vucyamānā</s>), should relinquish the matter — that is wholesome. If they do not relinquish it, those monks should be admonished and instructed up to the third time for the relinquishing of that matter. If, being admonished and instructed up to the third time, they relinquish that matter — that is wholesome. If they do not relinquish it and hold firmly to that matter, it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (offense requiring formal meeting).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA// uddānaṃ // [1] saṃcetanikā [2] hastagraho [3] obhāṣo [4] paricaryāvvaṇanaṃ [[5] saṃcaritraṃ [6-7] kuṭīvihārodve cā dūtena saṃghasya ca [10] bhedāyopakrāmati tasya [11] cānuvarttakāḥ [12] durvvacako [13] kuladūṣakāśca //
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>): [1] Intentional emission, [2] bodily contact, [3] lewd speech, [4] soliciting personal service, [5] acting as a go-between, [6-7] two rules on hut and <s>vihāra</s> building, [8] through a messenger, and [9] of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, [10] one who endeavors to cause a schism, [11] and his followers, [12] the difficult to admonish, and [13] the corrupters of families.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA// uddiṣtāḥ // kho punarāyuṣmanto trayodaśasaṃghātiśeṣo dharmāstatra nava prathamāpattikāścatvāro yāvantṛtīyakā yeṣāṃ bhikṣu anyatarāmāpattimāpatitvā yāvantakaṃ jānan[prati] cchādeti tāvantakaṃ tena bhikṣuṇā akāmaparivāsaṃ parivasitavyaṃ / parivuttha parivāsena bhikṣuṇā uttariṃ ṣaḍāhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghe mānatvaṃ caritavyaṃ / ciṇṇamānatve bhikṣūḥ kṛtānudharmo āhūyana prativedyeya asyā viṃśatigaṇo bhikṣū saṃgho tatra so bhikṣu āmreyitavyo / eka bhikṣuṇāpi vodūno viṃśatigaṇo bhikṣusaṃgho taṃ bhikṣumāmreya so ca bhikṣū anābhṛto te ca bhikṣū gārhyāḥ iyamatra sāmīcī /
body.translated_text: Recited, venerable ones, are the thirteen <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (offenses requiring formal meeting) rules. Of these, nine are first-offense rules and four are up-to-the-third-time rules. If a monk, having committed any one of these offenses, knowingly conceals it for as long as he does, for that same duration that monk must undergo involuntary probation (<s>parivāsa</s>). After completing the probation (<s>parivāsa</s>), that monk must further undergo six days of penance (<s>mānatva</s>) before the assembly of monks. After completing the penance (<s>mānatva</s>), the monk, having fulfilled the procedure, should be called and informed. A <s>Saṃgha</s> of twenty monks should be assembled there, and that monk should be rehabilitated. If the <s>Saṃgha</s> of twenty monks is short even by one monk when rehabilitating that monk, that monk is not rehabilitated, and those monks are blameworthy. This is the proper procedure herein.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_SA tatrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ dvitīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ tṛtīyamapi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ pariśuddhā atrāyuṣmanto yasmāttūṣṇīmevametaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Herein I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A third time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure herein; therefore they remain silent. Thus do I record it.

body.text: III. THE TWO ANIYATA DHARMAS
body.translated_text: III. THE TWO ANIYATA DHARMAS

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Aniy.ime kho punarāyuṣmanto duve aniyatā dharmā anvarddhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśamāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Now, venerable ones, the two <s>aniyata</s> (undetermined) rules come up for recitation every half-month in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of monastic rules) discourse.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Aniy.1. yo punabhikṣu mātugrāmeṇa sārddhaṃ praticchannāsane alaṅkarmāṇīye ekoyaraho niṣadyāṃ kalpeya tamena śraddheya vacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvā trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ manyatarānyatareṇa dharmeṇa vādeya pārāji kena vā saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā pācattikena vā niṣadyo bhikṣuḥ pratijānāmāno trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmanyatarānyatareṇa dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo pārājikena vā saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā pācattikena vā yena yena vā punarasya średdeya vacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvā dharmeṇa vadeya tena so bhikṣū dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo ayaṃ dharmo aniyato /
body.translated_text: If a monk should sit alone in private (<s>raho niṣadyā</s>) with a woman on a concealed seat suitable for the purpose, and a trustworthy female lay disciple (<s>upāsikā</s>), having seen him, should accuse him under any one of three rules — either <s>pārājika</s> (offense of defeat), or <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (offense requiring formal meeting), or <s>pācattika</s> (offense requiring confession) — the monk, if he acknowledges sitting there, should be dealt with under whichever one of the three rules applies: either <s>pārājika</s>, or <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>, or <s>pācattika</s>. Or by whatever rule the trustworthy female lay disciple (<s>upāsikā</s>), having seen him, accuses him, by that rule that monk should be dealt with. This rule is <s>aniyata</s> (undetermined).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Aniy.2. nāhaiva kho punaḥ praticchannāsanambhavati / nālaṃkarmaṇīyaṃ alaṃ kho puna mātṛgrāmaṃ dusthūlāya vācāya obhāsituṃ / pāpikāya maithunopasaṃhitāya tathārūpeca bhikṣū āsane mātṛgrāmeṇa sārddhaṃmeko ekāya raho niṣadyāṃ kalpeya tamenaṃ śraddheya vacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvādvinnāndharmāṇāṃ manyatarānyatareṇa dharmeṇa vadeya saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā // pācatti kena vā niṣadyāsbhikṣuḥ pratijānamāno dvinnāndharmāṇāmanyatarāntareṇa dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo / saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā / pācattikena vā / yena yena vā punarasya śraddheya vacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvā dharmeṇa vadeya tena tena so bhikṣū dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo ayaṃ pi dharmo aniyato //
body.translated_text: In this case, however, the seat is not concealed, nor suitable for the purpose, but it is suitable for addressing a woman with lewd words, wicked words connected with sexual intercourse. If a monk of such character should sit alone in private (<s>raho niṣadyā</s>) with a woman on such a seat, and a trustworthy female lay disciple (<s>upāsikā</s>), having seen him, should accuse him under either one of two rules — either <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (offense requiring formal meeting) or <s>pācattika</s> (offense requiring confession) — the monk, if he acknowledges sitting there, should be dealt with under whichever one of the two rules applies: either <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> or <s>pācattika</s>. Or by whatever rule the trustworthy female lay disciple (<s>upāsikā</s>), having seen him, accuses him, by that rule that monk should be dealt with. This rule too is <s>aniyata</s> (undetermined).

body.text: udyānaṃ // [1] praticchannāsanaṃ[2] rahoniṣaghāñca //
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>): [1] the concealed seat and [2] sitting alone in private.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Aniy.uddiṣtāḥ // kho punarāyuṣmanto duve aniyatā dharmā statrāyuṣmanto pracchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ dvitīyampi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāstutīyampi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ pariśuddhāḥ atrāyuṣmanto yasmāttūṣṇīmevametaṃ dhārayāmi //
body.translated_text: Recited, venerable ones, are the two <s>aniyata</s> (undetermined) rules. Herein I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A third time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure herein; therefore they remain silent. Thus do I record it.

body.text: IV. THE THIRTY NIHSARGIKA PACATTIKA DHARMAS.
body.translated_text: IV. THE THIRTY NIHSARGIKA PACATTIKA DHARMAS.

body.text: ime kho punarāyuṣmanto triṃśannissargiṃka pācattikā dharmā anvarddhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśamāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Now, venerable ones, the thirty <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offenses requiring forfeiture and confession) rules come up for recitation every half-month in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of monastic rules) discourse.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.1. kṛtacīvare hi bhikṣū hi uddhṛtasminkaṭhine daśāhaparamaṃ bhikṣuṇā atirekacīvarandhārayitavyaṃ / taduttarindhāreya nissargika pācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: When the robe-making of a monk is finished and the <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-frame) privileges have been withdrawn, an extra robe may be kept by a monk for ten days at most. If he keeps it beyond that, it is a <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.2. kṛtacīvare hi bhikṣū hi uddhṛtasminkaṭhine ekarātraṃ pi cetbhikṣu trayāṇāṃ cīvarāṇāṃ manyatarānyatareṇa vipravaseya anyatra saṃghasamutīye nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: When the robe-making of a monk is finished and the <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-frame) privileges have been withdrawn, if a monk should spend even one night separated from any one of his three <s>cīvaras</s> (robes), except with the consent of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, it is a <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.3. kṛtacīvare bhikṣu hi uddhṛtasminkaṭhine utpadyeya bhikṣusya akālacīvaramākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhṇitavyaṃ pratigṛhṇītvā kṣipra meva taṃ cīvaraṃ kārāpayitavyaṃ / kārāpayato ca tasya bhikṣūsya taṃ cīvaraṃ na paripūreya māsa paramantena bhikṣuṇā taṃ cīvaraṃ nikṣipitavyaṃ / ūnasya pāripūrīye santīye pratyāśāye taduttarinnikṣipeya santīye vā a santīye vā pratyāśāye nissargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: When the robe-making of a monk is finished and the <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-frame) privileges have been withdrawn, if out-of-season robe-cloth should arise for a monk, it may be accepted by a monk who desires it. Having accepted it, the robe should be made up quickly. If, while that monk is having the robe made up, the robe-cloth is not sufficient, that monk may store that robe-cloth for one month at most, for the purpose of completing what is deficient, provided there is expectation of obtaining more. If he stores it beyond that, whether or not there is expectation of obtaining more, it is a <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.4. yo punabhikṣūranyātikāye bhikṣuṇīye cīvaraṃ pratigṛhṇeya anyatra parivarttakena nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: If a monk should have a <s>cīvara</s> (robe) washed, dyed, or beaten by a nun who is not a relative, except in exchange, it is a <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.5. yo punabhikṣuranyātikāye bhikṣuṇīye purāṇacīvaradhovāyeya vā raṃjasyeya vā ākothopeya vā nissargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: If a monk should have an old <s>cīvara</s> (robe) washed, or dyed, or beaten by a nun who is not a relative, it is a <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.6. yo punabhikṣuranyātakaṃ gṛhapatiṃ vā gṛhapatiputraṃ vā cīvaraṃ yāceya anyatrasamaye nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: If a monk should ask for a <s>cīvara</s> (robe) from a householder or a householder's son who is not a relative, except at the proper occasion, it is a <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: tatrāyaṃ samayo acchinnacīvaro bhikṣūṃ bhavati / ayamatrasamayo /
body.translated_text: Herein, the proper occasion is this: when a monk's robe has been stolen or destroyed. This is the proper occasion herein.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.7. acchinnacīvareṇa bhikṣuṇā kṣamate anyātakaṃ gṛhapatimvā gṛhapatiputraṃ vā cīvaraṃ yācituṃ / tamenamabhibhāṣto sammato saṃbahule hi cīvare hi pravāreya tathā pravāritena bhikṣuṇā santarottaraparamaṃ cīvaraṃ sādayitavyaṃ taduttariṃ sādiyeya nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: If a monk whose robe has been stolen or destroyed is invited by a householder or a householder's son who is not a relative to accept robes, and is offered many robes, that monk so invited should accept robes to the value of an upper and lower garment at most. If he accepts beyond that, it is a <s>nissargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.8. bhikṣuṃ kho punaruddiśya anyatareṣāṃ dvinnāṃ gṛhipatikānāṃ cīvare cetāpanānyaḥ anyāni upasaṃskṛtāni bhavanti pratisaṃcetayitāni ime hi vayaṃ cīvaracetāpane hi civaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthannāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ cīvareṇācchādayiṣyāmaḥ / tatra ca bhikṣuḥ pūrvve apravārito upasaṃkramitvā vikalpamāpadyeya sādhu kho puna yūyaṃ māyuṣmanto ime hi cīvaracetāpane hi cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthaṃ nāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ cīvareṇācchādetha / evaṃrūpeṇa ca ubhau pi sahitau ekena kalyāṇakāmatāmupādāya pratiniṣpanne cīvare nisarggika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.8. If, with reference to a <s>bhikṣu</s>, two householders have robe-funds separately prepared and set aside [thinking]: 'Having procured a robe with these robe-funds, we shall clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so with a robe' — and if that <s>bhikṣu</s>, without having been previously invited, approaches them and makes a suggestion: 'It would be good indeed, venerable sirs, if you were to procure a robe with these robe-funds and clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so with a robe of such-and-such a kind' — and if in this manner both [householders] together, motivated by the desire for something fine, [produce a robe] — when the robe is finished, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.9. bhikṣuṃ kho punaruddiśya anyatareṣāṃ dvinnāṃ gṛhapatikasya gṛhapatinīye ca pratyeka cīvaracetāpanāni pratisaṃskṛtāni bhavanti pratisaṃcetāpitāni ime hi vayaṃ pratyeka cīvaracetāpane hi pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthaṃ nāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ cīvareṇācchādayisyāmaḥ / tatra ca bhikṣuḥ pūrvva apravārito upasaṃkramitvā vikalpamāpadyeya sādhu kho punastamāyuṣman tvaṃ ca bhagini ime hi pratyeka cīvara cetāpanehi pratyekaṃ cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā ityaṃ nāmaṃ bhiṃ pratyekaṃ cīvareṇācchādetha / evaṃ rūpeṇa vā evaṃ rūpeṇa vā ubhau pi sahitau / ekena kalyāṇakāmatāmupādāya pratiniṣpanne cīvare nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.9. If, with reference to a <s>bhikṣu</s>, two persons — a householder and a householder's wife — have separate robe-funds individually prepared and set aside [thinking]: 'Having procured a robe individually with these separate robe-funds, we shall individually clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so with a robe' — and if that <s>bhikṣu</s>, without having been previously invited, approaches them and makes a suggestion: 'It would be good indeed, venerable sir and sister, if you were to procure a robe individually with these separate robe-funds and clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so individually with a robe of such-and-such a kind' — and if in this manner or that manner both together, motivated by the desire for something fine, [produce a robe] — when the robe is finished, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.10. bhikṣu kho punaruddiśya anyataro rājā vā rājabhogyo vā dūtena cīvarace tāpanāni preṣeya so bhikṣustenopasaṃkramitvā taṃ bhikṣumevaṃ vadeya imāni khalvāryamuddiśya itthannāmena rājñā ca rājabhojyena vā dūtena cīvaracetāpanāni preṣitāni tāni āryo pratigṛhṇātu / tena bhikṣuṇā so dūto evamasya vacanīyo na kho punarāyuṣman kṣamate bhikṣusya cīvare cetāpanāni pratigṛhṇītuṃ / cīvarantu vayaṃ pratigṛhṇāmaḥ kālena samayena kalpikaṃ dīyamānaṃ / evamukto so dūto taṃ bhikṣumeva vādayanti / punarārya kecidbhikṣuṇāṃ vaiyāpṛtyaṅkaroti / ākāṃkṣāmaṇe na bhikṣuṇā santā vaiyāpṛtyaṃkaraṃ vyapadiśitavyāḥ / ārāmikā vā ete āyuṣman bhikṣuṇā vaiyāpṛtyaṃkarāye bhikṣuṇāṃ vaiyāpṛtyaṃ karonti / evamukto so dūto yena vaiyāpratyaṃkarāstenopasaṃkramitvā tanvaiyāpratyaṃkarānevaṃ vadeya sādhu kho puna yūyamāyuṣmanto vaiyāpratyaṃkarā ime hi cīvaracetāpane hi cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthaṃ nāma bhikṣuṃ cīvareṇācchādetha / kālena samayena kalpikenānavadyena so ca dūto tānvaiyāpṛtyaṃkarān saṃjñāpayitvā yena so bhikṣustenopasaṃkramitvā bhikṣūmeva vadeya ye khalu āryeṇa vaiyāpṛtyaṃkarā vyapadiṣṭāste mayā saṃjñāptāstāmupasaṃkrameyāmi ācchādayiṣyanti / te cīvareṇa kālena samayena kalpikenānavadyo na ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā cīvarānvikena te vaiyāpṛtyakarāstenopasaṃkramitvā te vaiyāpṛtyaṃkarāḥ / sakṛta dvitthikhutto tritthukhuto yācayitavyā vijñapayitavyāḥ / atho āyuṣmanto bhikṣusya cīvareṇa bhisakṛta dvikkhutto trikkhutto codayanto vijñāpayanto taṃ cīvaramabhiniṣpādeya ityetatkuśalannocedabhiniṣpādeya catukkhutto pañcakhutto ṣaḍkhutto paramantena bhikṣuṇā tūṣṇīṃ bhūtena uddeśe sthātavyaṃ / catukkhutto pañcakkhutto ṣaḍkkhatto paramaṃ tūṣṇībhūto uddeśe tiṣṭhanto taṃ cīvaramabhiniṣpādeya ityetatkuśalaṃ nocedabhiniṣpādeya taṃ duttayanto vācyāyamanto vātaṃ cīvaramabhiniṣpādeya abhiniṣpanne cīvare nissargika pācattikam / no cedabhiniṣpadeya yena setāni rājñā vā rājabhogyena vā itena cīvaracetāpanāni preṣitāni / tatra tena bhikṣuṇā svayaṃ vāganta vyaṃ / ito vā pratirūpo preṣayitavyo yāni kha āyuṣmanta hi itthaṃ nāmaṃ bhikṣūmuddiśya itena cīvaracetāpanāni preṣitāni na kha tāni tasya bhikṣusya kiñcidaththamkaronti / yuñjante yaḥ yathainaṃ sakaṃ dharmmā so vipraṇadhiśiṣyatīti iyamanusāmīcī /
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.10. If a king or a royal official sends robe-funds through a messenger with reference to a <s>bhikṣu</s>, that messenger should approach the <s>bhikṣu</s> and say: 'These robe-funds have been sent by the king or royal official named so-and-so through a messenger with reference to the venerable one. May the venerable one accept them.' That <s>bhikṣu</s> should say to the messenger: 'It is not proper, venerable sir, for a <s>bhikṣu</s> to accept robe-funds. But we do accept robes [themselves] when given at the proper time and occasion, and when they are allowable.' If the messenger so addressed says to the <s>bhikṣu</s>: 'But, venerable sir, is there anyone who serves the <s>bhikṣus</s> as an attendant?' — if he wishes, the <s>bhikṣu</s> should point out an attendant: 'These, venerable sir — the monastery attendants or the park-keepers — are those who serve the <s>bhikṣus</s> as attendants.' The messenger so addressed should approach the attendants and say: 'It would be good, venerable attendants, if you would procure a robe with these robe-funds and clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so with a robe at the proper time and occasion, with what is allowable and blameless.' And that messenger, having instructed those attendants, should approach that <s>bhikṣu</s> and say: 'The attendants whom the venerable one pointed out have been instructed by me. May the venerable one approach them; they will clothe you with a robe at the proper time and occasion, with what is allowable and blameless.' If the <s>bhikṣu</s> wishes [a robe], he should approach those attendants and prompt them once, twice, or three times, reminding and requesting: 'Venerable sirs, I am in need of a robe.' If by prompting and requesting once, twice, or three times, he obtains that robe — that is good. If he does not obtain it, he should stand silently at the assembly four times, five times, or six times at most. If by standing silently at the assembly four times, five times, or six times at most, he obtains that robe — that is good. If he does not obtain it, and if by pressing or speaking further he obtains that robe — when the robe is finished, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation). If he does not obtain it, then he should go himself or send a suitable [messenger] to the person — the king or royal official — by whom the robe-funds were sent, [saying]: 'The robe-funds which you, venerable sir, sent with reference to the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so — they have not benefited that <s>bhikṣu</s> in any way. May you take back what is your own; let it not be lost.' This is the proper procedure.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.uddānaṃ // [1] daśāhaṃ [2] vipravāso [3] akāle ca [4] pratigraho [5] dhovanā [6] yācanā [7-8] ciravarasāntarottaraṃ dve ca [9] vikalpena [10] rājā ca / prathamo vaggaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP. Summary verse: [1] ten days, [2] separation, [3] out of season, [4] acceptance, [5] washing, [6] requesting, [7-8] two [rules] concerning robe-funds from different [donors] combined, [9] by suggestion, [10] and the king. First section.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.11. yo punabhikṣuḥ śuddhakāṇakānāmeḍakalomānāṃnnavaṃ santhataṃ kārāpeya nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.11. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> has a new sitting mat (<s>santhata</s>) made of pure black sheep's wool, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.12. navaṃ santhataṃ bhikṣuṇā kārāpayamāṇenaśuddhakāṇakānāmeḍakalomānāṃ dve bhāgā ādayitavyāstṛtīyo odātikānāṃ catuttho gocarikāṇāṃ taduttarimādiyeya nissargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.12. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a new sitting mat made, two parts should be taken of pure black sheep's wool, the third of white, and the fourth of brown. If he takes more than that, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.13. yo punabhikṣūḥ kauśeya miśrāṇāmeḍaka lomānānnavaṃ santhataṃ kārāpeya nisargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.13. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> has a new sitting mat made of sheep's wool mixed with silk, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.14. navaṃ santhataṃ bhikṣuṇā kārāpayamāṇena prakāmaṃ ṣaḍvarṣāṇi dhārayitavyaṃ / tato ca bhikṣuḥ pratyottareṇa purāṇe santhataṃ visarjjayitvā vā avisarjjayitvā vā anyannavasanthataṃ kārāpeya kalyāṇakāmatāmupādeya anyatra samutīye nissargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.14. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a new sitting mat made, it must be kept for a full six years. If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, within that period, whether having discarded or not having discarded the old sitting mat, has another new sitting mat made — motivated by the desire for something fine, except with the consent of the <s>saṃgha</s> — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.15. navaṃ santhataṃ niṣīdanaṃ bhikṣuṇā kārāpayamāṇena, tato purāṇasanthatāto samantātsugatavitastinā bhāgo ādayitavyo navasya duvvaṇṇīkaraṇātha tato ca bhikṣuranādāya navasaṃtthataṃ niṣīdanaṃ kārāpeya nisarggika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.15. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a new sitting mat (<s>niṣīdana</s>) made, a piece measuring one <s>Sugata</s>-span on each side must be taken from the old sitting mat and incorporated [into the new one], for the purpose of disfiguring the new one. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, without taking [such a piece], has a new sitting mat made, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.16. bhikṣusya kho punaradhyānamāgge pratipannasya utpadyea eḍakalomāni ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhṇitavyaṃ hṇipratigṛtvā sāmaṃ triyojanaparamaṃ harttavyamante anyasmihārake taduttariṃ hāreyamante vā amante vā anyasmihārake nisargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.16. If sheep's wool becomes available to a <s>bhikṣu</s> while traveling on a journey, the <s>bhikṣu</s>, if he wishes, may accept it. Having accepted it, he may carry it himself for a maximum of three <s>yojanas</s>, when there is no one else to carry it. If he carries it beyond that, whether or not there is someone else to carry it, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.17. yo puna bhikṣuranyātikāye bhikṣuṇīye eḍakalomāni dhovāyeya vā raṃjāyeya vā / vijaṭāpayed vā nissargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.17. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> has sheep's wool washed, dyed, or carded by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who is not a relative, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.18. yo punabhikṣuḥ svahastaṃ jātarūparajatamudgṛhṇayeya vā udgṛhṇāyeya antamasato iha nikṣipehīti vā vadeya / upanikṣiptaṃ vā sādiyeya niḥssargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.18. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> accepts gold or silver with his own hand, or has [another] accept it, or even says 'deposit it here,' or approves of what has been deposited, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.19. yo punabhikṣuranekavidhaṃ kraya vikrayaṃ vyavahāraṃ samāpadyeya saṃyyathīdaṃ imaṃ kriṇa ito kriṇa ettaka settake krīṇāhīti vā vadeya niḥsargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.19. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> engages in various kinds of buying and selling transactions — such as saying 'buy this,' 'buy from here,' 'buy such-and-such for such-and-such [a price]' — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.20. yo punabhikṣuranekavidhaṃ jātarūparajatavikṛtivyavahāraṃ samāpadyeya niḥsargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.20. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> engages in various kinds of transactions involving gold or silver in worked forms, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.uddānaṃ / [11-12] śuddhakālakānāṃ dve bhāgā [13] kaiśeyamiśra [14] ṣaḍvarṣāṇi [15] niṣīdanaṃ [16] adhvānamāgo [17] vijaṭāpeya [18] svahastaṃ [19] krayavikraya [20] vikṛtivyavahāreṇa // dvitīyo vagaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP. Summary verse: [11-12] two parts of pure black [wool], [13] mixed with silk, [14] six years, [15] sitting mat, [16] on a journey, [17] having it carded, [18] with one's own hand, [19] buying and selling, [20] transactions in worked [gold and silver]. Second section.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.21. daśāhaparamaṃ bhikṣuṇā atirekapātraṃ dhārayitavyaṃ taduttariṃ dhāreya niḥssargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.21. A <s>bhikṣu</s> may keep an extra bowl for a maximum of ten days. If he keeps it beyond that, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.22. yo punabhikṣū unapañcavandhanavaddhena pātreṇa anyaṃ navaṃ pātraṃ paryāyeya imātāmupādāya / tena bhikṣuṇā taṃ pātraṃ bhikṣūparyāye niḥsaritavyaṃ / yo tahi bhikṣū paryāye pātraparyanto bhavati / so tasya bhikṣusya anupradātavyo / evaṃ te āyuṣmānpātro bhārayitavyo yāvadbhedana [nissargika] pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (<s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>) NP.22. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, having a bowl with fewer than five mends, seeks a new bowl in exchange — on this basis: that <s>bhikṣu</s> must forfeit that bowl to the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>. Whichever bowl is the last in the exchange among the <s>bhikṣus</s> — that should be given to that <s>bhikṣu</s> [saying]: 'This, venerable one, is your bowl; you must keep it until it breaks.' It is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (forfeiture with expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.23. yāni kho punarimāni gilānapratipeṣaṇīyāni bhaiṣajāni bhavanti / saṃyyathīdaṃ sapistailamadhuphāṇitaṃ / evaṃ rūpāṇi gilānena bhikṣuṇāmakṛtyābhigṛhītāni kṣamate / saptāhaṃ sannidhikāraṃ paribhujitaṃ / santaśeṣannissaritavyaṃ / taduttaritavyaṃ taduttariṃ khādeya vā bhuṃjeya vā santaśeṣanna nissareya niḥssargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 23. Now there are certain medicines for the care of the sick, namely: clarified butter (<s>sarpis</s>), oil, honey, and molasses (<s>phāṇita</s>). Such [medicines], received by a sick <s>bhikṣu</s> not through improper means, may be kept in storage and consumed for seven days. Whatever remains should be relinquished. If he goes beyond that — if he should eat or consume beyond that, or should not relinquish the remainder — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and confession).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.24. yo punabhikṣubhikṣusya cīvaraṃ dattvā yathāduṣto doṣātkupito anādamāno ācchāndeya vā ācchāndāpeya vā āhara[ti] bhikṣucīvaraṃ na te dademīti vā vadeya niḥsargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 24. If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, having given a robe to a <s>bhikṣu</s>, being corrupt, angry from hostility, displeased, should snatch it back or have it snatched back, or should say 'Give back the <s>bhikṣu's</s> robe! I will not give [it] to you!' — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.25. māso śeṣo grīṣmāṇomiti bhikṣuṇā varṣāśāṭikā cīvaraparyeṣitavyaṃ arddhamāso avaśiṣṭoti kṛtvā muṣitavyam // tato ca bhikṣuḥ pratyāṃtareṇa varṣāśāṭikā cīvaraṃ paryepeya kṛtvā vāstāyeya niḥ sargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 25. When one month of summer remains, a <s>bhikṣu</s> should seek a rains-bathing cloth (<s>varṣāśāṭikā</s> robe). When half a month remains, it should be sewn. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should seek or make a rains-bathing cloth robe before the proper time — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.26. yo punabhikṣūḥ svayaṃ yācikāya sūtrantantuvāyena cīvaraṃ dhunāyeya nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 26. If any <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a robe woven by a weaver by his own begging [for thread] — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.27. bhikṣūṃ kho punaruddhiśya anyataro gṛhapatirvvā gṛhapatiputro vā tantuvāyena cīvaraṃ dhunāyeya te eva bhikṣūḥ pūvve apravārito upasaṃkramitvā vikalpamāpadyeya sādhu kho punastamāyuṣmannimaṃ cīvaramāyataṃ ca karohi vistṛtaṃ ca karohi suvuttaṃ ca karohi / sutacchitaṃ ca karohi suvilikhitaṃ ca karohi / appeva nāma vayaṃ pi tavakiñcideva mātrāmupasaṃharema / māṣakamvā / māṣakārddhamvā piṇḍapātramvā piṇḍapātrāhimvā / tatra ca so bhikṣurevaṃ vaditvā na kiñcidevamātrāmupasaṃhareya / māṣakamvā / māṣakārddhamvā / piṇḍapātramvā piṇḍapātrāhimvā / abhiniṣpanne cīvare nisargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 27. If some householder or householder's son should have a robe woven by a weaver for a particular <s>bhikṣu</s>, and if that <s>bhikṣu</s>, not previously invited, should approach [the weaver] and make suggestions [saying]: 'Good sir, venerable one, make this robe long, make it wide, make it well-woven, make it well-cut, make it well-smoothed! Perhaps we too may bring something to you as a small gift — a <s>māṣaka</s> (coin), or half a <s>māṣaka</s>, or an alms-bowl, or more than an alms-bowl.' And if that <s>bhikṣu</s>, having spoken thus, should not bring even such a small gift — a <s>māṣaka</s>, or half a <s>māṣaka</s>, or an alms-bowl, or more than an alms-bowl — when the robe is completed, it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.28. daśāhānāgataṃ kho punatremāsaṃ kārtikī pauṇṇamāsī utpadyeya bhikṣūsya ātyāyikaṃ cīvaramatyāyikaṃ manyamāno na bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhṇitavyaṃ / pratigṛhṇitvā yāvancīvaradānakālasamayaṃ nikṣipitavyaṃ / taduttariṃ nikṣipeya nisargika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 28. If, ten days before the third month, the <s>Kārtikī</s> (October) full moon should arise, and an urgent robe should come to a <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>bhikṣu</s>, considering it urgent, should accept it. Having accepted it, he should keep it until the proper time for giving robes. If he keeps it beyond that — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.29. upavarṣa kho punaḥ tremāsaṃ kārtikī pauṇṇamāsī bhikṣucāraṇyake śayanāsane viharanti / samaye sapratibhaye / saśaṃka sammate / ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā trayāṇāṃ cīvarāṇāmanyatarānyataraṃ cīvaraṃ mantaragṛhe nikṣipitavyaṃ / syāttasyā bhikṣūsya kocideva pratyayo tasmāccīvarādvipravāsāya ṣaḍāhaparamantena bhikṣuṇā tasmāccīvarādvipravasitavyaṃ / taduttariṃ vipravaseya anyatra dīghīsamuteye nissarggika pācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 29. After the three months [of the rains retreat], after the <s>Kārtikī</s> full moon, when <s>bhikṣus</s> dwell in forest lodgings — [places that are] in season, fearful, and considered dangerous — a <s>bhikṣu</s> who so wishes may deposit any one of his three robes in an inner dwelling. If there is some reason for that <s>bhikṣu</s> to be separated from that robe, the <s>bhikṣu</s> may be separated from that robe for a maximum of six nights. If he is separated beyond that — except with the authorization of the <s>Saṃgha</s> — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.30. yo punabhikṣū jānan sāṃdhikāṃ lābhaṃ saṃghe pariṇatamātmano pariṇāmeya nissargika pācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargika Pācattika</s> 30. If any <s>bhikṣu</s>, knowingly, should divert to himself communal gains that have been designated for the <s>Saṃgha</s> — it is a <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.uddānaṃ / [21] pātra [22] bandhanaṃ [23] bhaiṣajña [24] mācchedo [25] varṣāśāṣṭikā [26-27] tantuvāyena dve [28] daśāhānāgata [29] mupavarṣa [30] pariṇāmanena tṛtīyo vagaḥ //
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>): [21] bowl, [22] mending, [23] medicine, [24] snatching back, [25] rains-bathing cloth, [26-27] two [rules] regarding the weaver, [28] ten days before [<s>Kārtikī</s>], [29] after the rains, [30] diverting [gains] — this is the third section.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_NP.uddiṣtāḥ / kho punaḥ rāyuṣmanto triṃśanniḥsarggika pācattikā dharmmāstatrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmikaccittha pariśuddhāḥ dvitīyampi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / tṛtiyampi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / pariśuddhātrāyuṣmanto yasmāttūṣṇīmevametaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the thirty <s>niḥsargika pācattika</s> rules have been recited. Therein I ask the venerable ones: 'Are you pure?' A second time I ask the venerable ones: 'Are you pure?' A third time I ask the venerable ones: 'Are you pure?' The venerable ones herein are pure, since they are silent — thus I understand it.

body.text: V. THE NINETY-TWO PACATTIKA DHARMAS.
body.translated_text: V. THE NINETY-TWO <s>PĀCATTIKA</s> RULES.

body.text: ime kho punarāyuṣmanto dvānavatiṃ śuddhapācattikā dharmā anvarddhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśamāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these ninety-two pure <s>pācattika</s> rules come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> sūtra every half-month.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Pāc.1. saṃprajānamṛṣāvāde pācattikam /
