PrMoSū(Mā)_Śai.66. na udake uccāraṃ vā praśrāvaṃ vā kheḍḍaṃ vā siṃhāṇakaṃ vā agilāno kariṣyāmīti śikṣākaraṇīyā /
PrMoSū(Mā)_Śai.67. na sthito uccāramvā praśrāvamvā agilāno kariṣyāmīti śikṣākaraṇīyā /
body.translated_text: Training rule: "I will not teach <s>Dharma</s> to one holding a weapon" — this is a <s>śaikṣa</s> (training rule) to be trained in. Training rule: "I will not teach <s>Dharma</s> to one holding a stick" — this is a <s>śaikṣa</s> (training rule) to be trained in. Training rule: "I will not teach <s>Dharma</s> to one holding an umbrella" — this is a <s>śaikṣa</s> (training rule) to be trained in. Training rule: "I will not, being off the path, teach <s>Dharma</s> to one on the path" — this is a <s>śaikṣa</s> (training rule) to be trained in. Training rule: "I will not defecate or urinate on green grass" — this is a <s>śaikṣa</s> (training rule) to be trained in. Training rule: "I will not defecate or urinate in water" — this is a <s>śaikṣa</s> (training rule) to be trained in. Training rule: "I will not defecate or urinate while standing" — this is a <s>śaikṣa</s> (training rule) to be trained in.

body.text: uddānam // [58-59] na śastrāyudha [60] daṇḍa [61] cchatra [62] utpatha [63] pṛṣṭhato [64] yānaṃ [65] haritaṃ[66] udaka [67] sthitena / ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ //
body.translated_text: Summary verse: [58] weapon, [59] stick, [60] umbrella, [61] sword, [62] off the path, [63] on green grass, [64] in water, [65] standing, [66] not on a high place, [67] not from a cliff — the sixth section.

body.text: uddiṣtāḥ kho punarāyuṣmanto sātirekapañcāśata śaikṣādharmāḥ / tatrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / dvitīyampi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / tṛtīyampi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / pariśuddhāḥ atrāyuṣmanto yasmāttūṣṇīmevametandhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the <s>śaikṣa</s> (training) rules have been recited. I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask: are you pure in this matter? A third time I ask: are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, therefore they are silent — thus I understand this.

body.text: VIII. THE SEVEN ADHIKARANA SAMATHA DHARMAS.
body.translated_text: VIII. THE SEVEN ADHIKARANA SAMATHA DHARMAS.

body.text: ime kho punarāyuṣmanto sapta adhikaraṇasamathādharmā anvardhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśamāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these seven <s>adhikaraṇasamatha</s> (dispute settlement) <s>dharmas</s> come up for recitation every half-month in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of monastic rules).

body.text:
PrMoSū(Mā)_AŚ.1. ye utpannotpannānāmadhikaraṇānāṃ śamathāya vyapaśamathāya sanvakṛte / saṃyyathīdaṃ saṃmukhavinayo śamatho /
PrMoSū(Mā)_AŚ.2. smṛtivinayo śamatho /
PrMoSū(Mā)_AŚ.3. amūḍhavinayo śamatho /
PrMoSū(Mā)_AŚ.4. pratijñākārako śamatho /
PrMoSū(Mā)_AŚ.5. tasya pāpeyasiko śamatho /
PrMoSū(Mā)_AŚ.6. yo bhūyasiko śamatho /
PrMoSū(Mā)_AŚ.7. tṛṇaprastārako ca śamatho / saptamo /
body.translated_text: The seven <s>adhikaraṇasamatha</s> (dispute settlement) <s>dharmas</s> are: <s>saṃmukhavinaya</s> (face-to-face settlement) should be given; <s>smṛtivinaya</s> (settlement by recollection) should be given; <s>amūḍhavinaya</s> (settlement for one no longer insane) should be given; <s>pratijñākāraka</s> (settlement by confession) should be applied; the decision by majority (<s>yobhūyasika</s>) should be applied; the decision regarding the worse nature of the offense (<s>tasyapāpeyasika</s>) should be applied; <s>tṛṇaprastāraka</s> (covering over with grass) should be applied.

body.text: uddiṣtāḥ kho punarāyuṣmanto sapta adhikaraṇasamathādharmā sūtrā yuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / dvitīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / tṛtīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / pariśuddhāḥ atrāyuṣmanto yasmāttūṣṇīmevametaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the seven <s>adhikaraṇasamatha</s> (dispute settlement) <s>dharmas</s> have been recited. I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask: are you pure in this matter? A third time I ask: are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, therefore they are silent — thus I understand this.

body.text: ime kho punarāyuṣmanto duve dharmāḥ / dharmo anudharmaśu anvardhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśamāgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, this is the <s>dharma</s> (doctrine) and <s>anudharma</s> (subsidiary doctrine) that should be known.

body.text: tatra dharmo nāma yamubhayato vinayo / anudharmo nāma yā atra pratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s> is well-spoken, <s>anudharma</s> is that which follows it; the practice in accordance with <s>dharma</s> and <s>anudharma</s> is the path to the cessation of suffering.

body.text: uddiṣtāḥ kho punarāyuṣmanto duve dharmāḥ / dharmo anudharmaśu tetrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / dvitīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ tṛtīyampi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ / pariśuddhāḥ atrāyuṣmanto yasmāttūṣṇīmevametaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the <s>dharma</s> and <s>anudharma</s> have been recited. I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask: are you pure in this matter? A third time I ask: are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, therefore they are silent — thus I understand this.

body.text: uddiṣṭaṃ / kho punarāyuṣmanto prātimokṣasya vastu / uddiṣṭaṃ nidānaṃ / uddiṣṭāścatvāraḥ pācattikā dharmāḥ / uddiṣtā trayodaśasaṃghātiśeṣāḥ dharmāḥ / uddiṣtāḥ duve aniyatā dharmāḥ / uddiṣṭā triṃśannisargikapācattikā dharmāḥ / uddiṣtā dvānavati śuddha pacattikā dharmāḥ / uddiṣtāḥ catvāraḥ prātideśanikā dharmāḥ / uddiṣtāḥ sātirekapaścāṣaḍ śaikṣā dharmāḥ / uddiṣtāssaptadhikaraṇaśamathādharmāḥ / uddiṣtā duve dharmāḥ / dharmo anudharmaśu / etakoyaṃ punastasya bhagavato tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyak saṃbuddhasya dharmavinayo prātimokṣasūtrāgato sūtraparyāpanno yo vā anyopi kaściddharmasya anudharmo tatra samagre hi sarvve hi sahite hi saṃmodamāne hi avivadamāne hi ekoddeśe hi kṣīrodakī kṛtehi śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ dīpayamāne hi / sukhañca phāsuñca viharante hi anadhyāvācāya śikṣākaraṇīyā /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (code of monastic rules) has been recited — the introduction, four <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) rules, thirteen <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> (rules entailing formal meeting of the community) rules, two <s>aniyata</s> (undetermined) rules, thirty <s>niḥsargika-pāyattika</s> (rules entailing forfeiture and expiation) rules, ninety-two <s>pāyattika</s> (expiation) rules, four <s>pratideśanīya</s> (rules requiring confession) rules, the <s>śaikṣa</s> (training) rules, the seven <s>adhikaraṇasamatha</s> (dispute settlement) rules, and <s>dharma</s> and <s>anudharma</s>. This is the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. Let us all train in these rules together, in concord, without dispute, as milk mixes with water, dwelling in comfort.

body.text:
PrMoSū(Mā)_Schlußv.1. kṣāntiḥ paramantapo titikṣā nirvvāṇaṃ paramaṃ vadanti buddhāḥ /
nahi pravrajitaḥ paropaghātī śravaṇo bhoti parānviheṭhayantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Patience and forbearance is the supreme austerity, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the highest, say the <s>Buddhas</s>; one who injures another is not a renunciant, one who harms another is not an ascetic.

body.text: idamtasya bhagavato vipaścitasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasva acirābhisaṃbuddhasya nirarbbude bhikṣusaṃghe saṃkṣiptena prātimokṣaṃ subhāṣitam //
body.translated_text: This was spoken by the Blessed One, the fully enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s> <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Schlußv.2. āropavādī aparopaghātī pratimokṣe ca samvare mātrajñatā ca / bhuktismiṃ prāntañca śayanāsanaṃ adhicitte cāyogo etaṃ buddhānuśāsanaṃ //
body.translated_text: Guarding speech, well-restrained in mind, one should not do unwholesome deeds with the body; one should purify these three courses of action, and attain the path declared by the Sage.

body.text: idaṃ tasya bhagavato śaikṣisya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya acirābhisaṃbuddhasya nirarbbude bhikṣusaṃghe saṃkṣiptena prātimokṣaṃ subhāṣitam //
body.translated_text: This was spoken by the Blessed One, the fully enlightened <s>Śikhin</s> <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Schlußv.3. adhicetasi mā pramādyate munino maunapadeṣuśikṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not be negligent in the higher mind; be a sage wise in the teaching of the sages;

children.text: śokāḥ na bhavanti tāyino upaśāntasya sadāsmṛtīmataḥ //
children.translated_text: With sorrows ended, free from distress — the protector who is always mindful attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: idaṃ tasya bhagavate viśvabhuvasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyak saṃbuddhasya nirarbbude bhikṣusaṃghe saṃkṣiptena pratimokṣaṃ subhāṣitaṃ //
body.translated_text: This was spoken by the Blessed One, the fully enlightened <s>Viśvabhū</s> <s>Buddha</s>.

children.translated_text: Not to do any evil, to accomplish the good,
To purify one's own mind — this is the teaching of all the <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: idantasya bhagavato krukrucchandasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyak saṃbuddhasya acirābhisaṃbuddhasya nirarbbude bhikṣusaṃghe saṃkṣiptena pratimokṣaṃ subhāṣitaṃ //
body.translated_text: This was spoken by the Blessed One, the fully enlightened <s>Krakucchanda</s> <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text:
PrMoSū(Mā)_Schlußv.5. yathāhi bhramaro puṣpamvaṇṇagandhagaheṇyaṃ
paraiti rasamādāya evaṃ grāme muniścaret /
body.translated_text: Just as a bee takes from a flower its color and fragrance without harming the flower's beauty,

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Schlußv.6. na pareṣāṃ vilomāni na pareṣāṃ kṛtākṛtam /
children.translated_text: So should the sage go through the village. One should not look at the faults of others,
Nor at what others have done or not done; one should examine one's own deeds, done and undone.

body.text: idantasya bhagavato konākamunisya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya acirābhisaṃbuddhasya nirarbbude bhikṣusaṃghe saṃkṣiptena pratimokṣaṃ subhāṣitam /
body.translated_text: This was spoken by the Blessed One, the fully enlightened <s>Konākamuni</s> <s>Buddha</s>.

children.translated_text: There is no <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) without <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), no <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) without <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation);

children.text: yasya dhyānañca prajñā ca sa vai nirvāṇasya antike //
children.translated_text: He who possesses <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), he is truly near <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: tatrāyamādi bhavati / iha prajñasya bhikṣuṇo indriyaiguptiḥ saṃjñaptiḥ prātimokṣe ca saṃvaro //
body.translated_text: Herein this is the beginning: for the wise <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), there is guarding of the sense faculties, mindful awareness, and restraint in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code).

children.translated_text: One should always cultivate what is wholesome, living purely and diligently,
and being one who spreads out bedding properly, one who is skilled in right conduct.

body.text: tataḥ prāmodya bahulo bhikṣurnirvāṇasyeva antike //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), filled with joy, is truly near <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: idaṃ tasya bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya acirābhisaṃbuddhasya nirarbbude bhikṣusaṃghe saṃkṣiptena prātimokṣaṃ subhāṣitam //
body.translated_text: This is the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code) of the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the Perfectly Awakened One, who recently attained full awakening — well-spoken in brief for the community of monks that was free from discord.

children.text: PrMoSū(Mā)_Schlußv.9. cakṣuṣā saṃvaraḥ sādhuḥ sādhuḥ śrotreṇa saṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Restraint by the eye is good; good is restraint by the ear;
restraint by the nose is good; good is restraint by the tongue;

children.text: kāyena saṃvaraḥ sādhu manasā sādhu saṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: restraint by the body is good; good is restraint by the mind;
the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who is restrained in all respects is released from all <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering).

body.text: idantasya bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ śākyādhirājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyak sambuddhasya acirābhisaṃbuddhasya nirarbbude bhikṣusaṃghe saṃkṣiptena pratimokṣaṃ subhāṣitam /
body.translated_text: This is the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code) of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the supreme lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the Perfectly Awakened One, who recently attained full awakening — well-spoken in brief for the community of monks that was free from discord.
These are the <s>Prātimokṣas</s> (monastic codes) of the glorious Perfectly Awakened Ones; proclaimed [lacuna]

body.text: [1] vipaśvī ānāyavadyañca [2] śikhī prakāśayati adhicittañca [3] viśvabhuḥ / akaraṇañca pāpānāṃ [4] krukrucchandaḥ / duryāñca [5] konākamuniḥ / [6] dhyānāni ca kāśyapo prakāśayati [7] saṃvaraṃ śākyamuneḥ / ete saptadaśabalā / mahāprajñā amitabuddhī saptānāṃ samyak saṃbuddhānāṃ....nā....śyā....dhipatīnāṃ dharmākhyānāni uktāni / uddistaṃ prātimokṣasūtraṃ / kṛtaṃ saṃghena yo ca dha....āryāḥ....pālayantu / samāptaṃ / prātimokṣasūtraṃ āryamahāsāṃghikānāṃ lokottaravādināṃ mādhyāddeśikānāṃ pāṭhi.... / ye dharmahetuprabhavā taṃ pi tathāgato avadatteṣāñca yonirodhaṃ evaṃ vādī mahāśravaṇaḥ / ye dharmmo yaṃ pravaramahāyāna payiśya śākyabhikṣuloka .... /
body.translated_text: [1] <s>Vipaśvī</s> proclaimed blamelessness; [2] <s>Śikhī</s> illuminates higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>); [3] <s>Viśvabhū</s> proclaimed the non-doing of evil; [4] <s>Krakucchanda</s> proclaimed endurance; [5] <s>Konākamuni</s> proclaimed [restraint]; [6] <s>Kāśyapa</s> illuminates the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations); [7] <s>Śākyamuni</s> proclaimed restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). These seven possess the ten powers, great wisdom, and immeasurable intelligence. Of the seven Perfectly Awakened Ones, [lacuna] the lords — their proclamations of the <s>Dharma</s> have been spoken. The <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (monastic code scripture) has been recited. It has been performed by the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community); and whatever [lacuna] — may the Noble Ones preserve it. Concluded. The <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> of the Noble <s>Mahāsāṃghikas</s> (Great Assembly), the <s>Lokottaravādins</s> (Transcendentalists), of the Middle Country tradition [lacuna]. Whatever <s>dharmas</s> arise from causes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their origin and also their cessation — thus speaks the Great Ascetic. This <s>Dharma</s>, the excellent <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) [lacuna] the <s>Śākya</s> monk community [lacuna].

body.text: śākyabhikṣu śrīvijayabhadralikhitamidam //
body.translated_text: This was written by the <s>Śākya</s> monk <s>Śrīvijayabhadra</s>.
